channel.title: HumanSounding: this week in AI writing
channel.description: The weekly column on AI's accent: what's rising, what's fading, and what changed in the machine vernacular.

item.title: The Load-Bearing Tic, Now With a Growth Chart
item.description: A new GitHub study quantifies Claude's favorite catchphrase, while OpenAI tunes two of its own tells out of ChatGPT.

item.title: Claude Opus 5's New Tic: Everything Is "Load-Bearing"
item.description: A single overused metaphor turned into a developer meme this week, showing how AI writing tells are model-specific and short-lived.

item.title: Why do AI-writing checkers miss the most obvious AI writing?
item.description: Six regular expressions, validated on thirteen of thirteen positives, found none of the thirty-seven instances a reader found in the same fifteen documents.

item.title: Do AI-writing checkers agree with each other? I tested three
item.description: Two independent rule sets, run over the same 456 documents, reproduce three findings from the corpus study. Both also contain the same measurement mistake.

item.title: Why does AI keep apologizing and rating its own answers?
item.description: AI prose addresses an evaluator, human prose addresses a reader. Six shapes that habit takes, and a one-second test for catching it.

item.title: Do all AI models write the same way? I measured four
item.description: 160 documents, four models, one pre-ChatGPT human baseline. Em dashes are a Claude habit, the delve vocabulary is a Gemini habit, and no rule describes AI writing in general.

item.title: The Em Dash Retired. Nine New Tells Took Its Place.
item.description: A viral checklist of post-em-dash writing tics shows AI-detection folklore evolving as fast as the models it tracks.

item.title: Why AI Loves the Em Dash: The Markdown Theory
item.description: New research ties AI's em-dash habit to markdown training, while Wikipedia officially names the 'not X, it's Y' tell.

item.title: I had an AI build a website that catches AI writing
item.description: The build log behind this site: the weekly robot, the honesty rules, and the embarrassing parts.

item.title: Claude now watermarks its text. Here's what that changes.
item.description: The invisible mark proves a model touched the text, and nothing more. What writers should and shouldn't worry about.

item.title: This week in AI writing: August 10, 2026
item.description: HumanSounding launched: the live trend board, the in-browser draft checker, and downloadable instruction files for Claude, ChatGPT, and Gemini. • The first autonomous research run added a new rising tell: lighter punctuation with longer, comma-sparse sentences in newer models. • Wikipedia's editor guide now flags Grok-specific vocabulary (causal, empirical, correlate); added to the trend board. • A July 2026 analysis found that among major chatbots only Claude still uses em dashes above the professional human rate; GPT-5.4 now sits below it. • EQ-Bench weights the "not just X, but Y" pattern at 25% of its slop score, with models running far above the human rate (EQ-Bench, Jul 2026). • We audited our own pages with Impeccable, a detector for AI design tells: 70 findings, including 42 em dashes on the site that lectures about em dashes. All fixed, along with every contrast shortfall it caught.
